hero.eyebrow: Automation infrastructure · APIs · bots · CRM workflows
hero.title: I build the backend that lets small teams operate like bigger ones.
hero.subtitle: Bots, APIs, webhooks, CRM flows, and internal tools—designed as one dependable system. For always-on workloads, I can run multiple services on a managed Oracle Cloud server instead of scattering them across separate hosting plans.

primaryCta.label: Tell me what needs to run

infrastructure.intro: Oracle Cloud is still cloud infrastructure—but I manage the operating system and service layer directly. That gives an operation one place for its always-on APIs, bots, workers, logs, secrets, and deployments.
infrastructure.plainLanguage: Think of it as a secure computer that stays online in the cloud. I install each service, keep it running, restart it automatically if it fails, and expose only the endpoints the business actually needs.

options.label: My managed-VM approach
options.title: Shared infrastructure you control
items: Several APIs, bots, and workers can share one compute allocation
A predictable server-cost baseline for steady, always-on workloads
Direct control of processes, logs, environment variables, and networking
Best fit when services need to stay online and work together continuously

options.label: Managed platforms / serverless
options.title: Fast deployment with platform abstraction
items: Convenient for prototypes, isolated apps, and bursty or short-lived workloads
Costs can grow across services, execution, build minutes, or usage tiers
Less operating-system work, with less low-level control in return
A useful option when speed-to-deploy matters more than consolidating services

infrastructure.note: The right hosting choice depends on workload and traffic. I use the managed-VM model where consolidation, control, and an always-on cost baseline create a practical advantage—not because every project belongs on one server.

featuredCase.title: A multi-service operations stack on one Oracle Cloud host.
featuredCase.summary: I built and operate an Ubuntu-based environment for Discord automation, API endpoints, background jobs, and admin tooling. Instead of treating every bot as a separate hosting product, the services share a controlled infrastructure layer with individual process boundaries.

about.title: I’m most useful when the tools already exist—but the system between them does not.
about.body: I focus on the operational layer behind the interface: what happens after a form is submitted, a customer replies, a Discord command runs, an API fails, or a process restarts. My goal is a setup the team can understand, operate, and grow without adding unnecessary complexity.
